s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the forearm with a firm, non-tender mass and cortical bone lysis
salient_findings: Progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of the forearm
Firm, non-tender 4 × 5 cm mass in the subcutaneous tissues
Cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna on radiographs
Mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues on MRI
key_facts: No family history of similar lesions
Normal neurovascular examination of the hand
Soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity on radiographs
Mass isointense to muscle on T1-weighted MRI
Cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement and a mass that is isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration are consistent with osteosarcoma, a common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Ewing's sarcoma is also a primary malignant bone tumor, it typically presents with systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Chondrosarcoma is more common in older adults and typically presents with a slower growing mass, which does not fit the rapid progression in this 9-year-old girl.

rejected.label: Adamantinoma
rejected.why: Adamantinoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the tibia and has a distinct appearance on imaging, which does not match the description provided.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumor is typically seen in skeletally mature individuals and has a characteristic 'soap bubble' appearance on radiographs, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cyst is a benign lesion that typically presents with a fluid-fluid level on MRI, which is not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastoma is a rare benign tumor that typically presents with a smaller, well-defined mass, which does not fit the description of the large, aggressive mass in this case.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the spine or base of the skull, which does not match the location of the mass in this case.
